📍 Where AI Assistants Find Local Businesses (2026)

When someone asks an AI assistant for a local plumber, roofer, or dentist, the assistant points to websites. A November 2026 study measured which sites get cited — and it is not only your own site.

Home › Guides

When a customer asks ChatGPT, Gemini, or another AI assistant for a local plumber or dentist, the assistant names websites. Those named sites are called citations. They show you where the assistant is looking.

The numbers on this page come from AI Syndicate Research's AI Local Report, November 2026. Researchers asked 12 AI assistants 147,600 questions across 4,100 local markets in all 50 US states. Every figure below is from that report.

What the report found

Most of the time, the assistant is not pointing at a shop's own website.

About 1,200 review sites, directories, "best of" lists and forums — each one cited in five or more markets — took 57% of all 331,925 citations.

Yelp was the most-cited site, at 5.6%. It led in 8 of the 20 trades the report broke out. The next most-cited sites were:

  • Google (Maps and Business Profile links): 3.1%
  • Facebook: 2.5%
  • Angi: 2.2%
  • Reddit: 2.1%

No single site reaches 6% of citations. A typical market draws on 36 different source sites. What comes first depends on the trade. In 12 of 20 trades, a site made for that trade was cited more than Yelp.

The report lists the most-cited site, and the next two, for each of 20 trades. The share is of all citations in that trade. The report leaves a ranked business's own website, and dictionary sites used to define a word, out of this list.

Where to get listed first

Start with the sites the report says get cited most. Then check the table for your trade.

  1. Get on Yelp and keep the listing accurate. Yelp was the most-cited site in the report (5.6%) and the top site in 8 of 20 trades, including HVAC, electricians, roofing, garage door repair, pest control, med spas, cosmetic dentists, and water damage restoration.
  2. Claim your Google Business Profile. Google Maps and Business Profile links were the second most-cited source, at 3.1% of all citations.
  3. Keep a current Facebook page. Facebook was third, at 2.5% of citations.
  4. Get listed on Angi if you do home-service work. Angi was 2.2% of all citations. It was the most-cited site for plumbers (7.5%), and it is in the next two for electricians, HVAC, pest control, roofing, and window and door replacement.
  5. Be findable in Reddit threads about your trade. Reddit was 2.1% of citations. The report notes that reviews and Reddit matter across trades. That does not mean Reddit works like a directory you can simply claim.
  6. Get on the directory that leads in your trade. For many trades, a specialist site leads: Carfax for auto repair, Justia or Super Lawyers for legal work, Zillow and Realtor.com for real estate, EnergySage for solar, Tripadvisor for hotels and restaurants, MoveBuddha for movers, and EcoWatch for window and door replacement. Use the table above.
  7. Then make sure you can catch the work. Being listed only helps if you answer when the job comes in. See our 24/7 phone receptionists and the free "Is your website leaking jobs?" audit. Trade tool guides: plumbers, HVAC, electricians, roofers, garage door companies, pest control, med spas, and law firms.
Source: AI Syndicate Research, "AI Local Report, November 2026," measured 1–9 November 2026. Read the full report at aisyndicate.com.

FAQ

Which websites do AI assistants cite for local businesses?In AI Syndicate's November 2026 AI Local Report, about 1,200 review sites, directories and other platforms, each cited in five or more markets, took 57% of 331,925 citations. Yelp was the most-cited site, at 5.6%.
Is a Google Business Profile enough?No. Google Maps and Business Profile links were 3.1% of citations — second after Yelp at 5.6%. The report says more than half of citations go to about 1,200 review sites, directories and lists, and that a trade's own directory often matters more.
Do the same sites matter for every trade?No. Yelp led in 8 of 20 trades. In the other 12, a trade-specific site led — for example Carfax for auto repair, Justia for most legal trades, Zillow for real estate, and EnergySage for solar.
